chief_complaint: Chronic musculoskeletal pain (low back and hand osteoarthritis) with metabolic risk factors (obesity, hypertension, prediabetes)
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 58-year-old white male with a long-standing history of obesity since 2001, hand osteoarthritis diagnosed in 2012, and chronic low back pain beginning in 2014. Anemia and prediabetes were identified in 2017. Blood pressure measured at 130/90 mmHg classifies as stage 2 hypertension. In 2021 he reported increased stress and transitioned to part‑time employment. He has been seen primarily for wellness visits (9) and a few outpatient encounters, with no emergency or inpatient care. His only prescribed medication is naproxen 220 mg for hand osteoarthritis, indicating limited pharmacologic management of his hypertension, metabolic risk, and anemia.

active_problems.name: Localized primary osteoarthritis of the hand

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include multiple medication review reminders (2020‑2021), prior full‑time employment, episodes of social isolation (resolved 2018‑2021), viral sinusitis (2019), and gingival disease/gingivitis (2018).

active_medications.name: Naproxen sodium 220 MG Oral Tablet
active_medications.purpose: Pain control for hand osteoarthritis (and other musculoskeletal pain)

social_determinants: Part‑time employment since 2021, higher education (college degree), recent increase in psychosocial stress, no documented smoking or alcohol use, and limited socioeconomic detail that may affect access to care and healthy lifestyle resources.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure 130/90 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension); BMI documented as ≥30 (obesity) but numeric value missing; A1c 6.0% (prediabetic); anemia present; only one medication (NSAID) increasing renal and cardiovascular risk; lipid panel, eGFR, and smoking/alcohol/physical activity data are absent; Charlson comorbidity index 1; overall clinical complexity moderate.

Lipid panel results missing; needed for ASCVD risk calculation.
Renal function (eGFR) not recorded; important given NSAID use and hypertension.
Family history of cardiovascular disease, diabetes, or kidney disease not provided.
Immunization records (influenza, COVID‑19, pneumococcal, shingles) absent.
No iron studies, B12, folate, or stool occult blood results to determine anemia etiology.
Only a single BP reading available; longitudinal trend needed for hypertension management.
No information on over‑the‑counter NSAID use or adherence to naproxen.

clinical_impression: The patient presents with a high‑risk metabolic‑cardiovascular profile (obesity, stage 2 hypertension, prediabetes) compounded by chronic musculoskeletal pain and anemia. NSAID therapy for osteoarthritis adds renal and blood‑pressure concerns. Gaps in key laboratory data (lipids, renal function, anemia work‑up) and limited pharmacologic management suggest under‑treated chronic disease and potential for future cardiovascular and renal complications.
